page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-1 is an arm64-based instance powered by a single dedicated physical core of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It features 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-threaded execution and multi-threaded or memory-intensive operations. The instance achieves strong performance in single-threaded compression tasks, with gzip compression reaching 32.1 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.05 GB/sec. However, due to its single-vCPU limitation, multi-core stress-ng performance is poor, matching its single-core score of 1801.88. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth at 29.49 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 11.76 GB/sec. Passmark CPU scores and database operations are weak to poor, and Redis SET operations are limited to 2.27 million operations per second.

The c4a-highmem-1 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. The primary tradeoff is the strict single-vCPU limit, which severely restricts multi-threaded scaling, database throughput, and web serving capacity, as evidenced by a static web serving throughput of 2.78 GB/sec. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, small-scale caching, basic memory-intensive background tasks, or minor text processing and low-demand single-threaded utilities.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-1 is a memory-optimized arm64 instance featuring a single dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 core running at 3.0 GHz and 8.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on its high memory-to-vCPU ratio to support memory-bound workloads. Performance benchmarks show strong single-threaded capabilities, particularly in compression and decompression tasks. However, the single-core configuration imposes significant limitations, resulting in poor multi-core and database performance, as well as constrained memory write bandwidth. This instance represents a qualitatively cost-efficient option for lightweight, memory-intensive applications that do not require parallel processing. It is best suited for single-threaded utilities, small-scale caching, and basic background tasks.
